paper_title: MMSearch-OPD: Easy Made Hard, Hard Made Learnable for Long-Horizon Multimodal Search Agents

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing imagequestion pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Multimodal deep search agents address knowledgeintensive visual questions through interleaved reasoning and external retrieval (Wu et al., 2025; Geng et al., 2025). Recent advances move toward longhorizon investigation, connecting evidence across webpages and using acquired visual observations to guide subsequent searches (Huang et al., 2026; Du et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2026b). Two challenges limit training for this setting. Existing multimodal datasets contain many questions solvable through parametric knowledge or short retrieval, while constructing harder questions through 1 graph composition and visual enrichment entails relation collection, image curation, and evidence validation (Chen et al., 2026; Chu et al., 2026; Zhang et al., 2026b). Reusing existing imagequestion pairs offers starting point for constructing questions with greater search demands. Meanwhile, useful long-horizon investigation may end in redundant verification, premature stopping, or an incorrect answer. Terminal rewards provide limited process feedback, and trajectory-level advantages supply shared scalar signal throughout rollout (Shao et al., 2024). Identical returns also remove group-relative learning contrast. Process rewards and teacher guidance address these limitations (Chen et al., 2026; Li et al., 2026); we combine outcome-based optimization with selective token-level teacher guidance. To address these challenges, we propose MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable question refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline reuses simple multimodal questions and their candidate reasoning chains. Expand extends chain depth, Blur increases disambiguation requirements, and Visualize introduces retrievable visual evidence. These configurable operators control the intended evidence requirements while reusing seed assets (Figure 1). After question validation and supervised initialization, joint training combines answer rewards and behavior penalties with tokenlevel OPD on imperfect student trajectories. The shaped reward gap adjusts guidance strength, while an exponential schedule reduces the OPD coefficient as training proceeds. Our contributions are summarized as follows: We introduce Refine, pipeline that reuses existing multimodal questions and adjusts their evidence requirements through chain expanFigure 1: Motivation for MMSearch-OPD and an example of Refine for long-horizon multimodal search. sion, entity disambiguation, and visual evidence requirements. We develop joint RL and selective OPD training that combines answer rewards and behavior penalties with reward-gap-weighted token guidance and exponential annealing on imperfect long-horizon search trajectories. We organize evaluation across ten multimodal search benchmarks to assess agent performance and the roles of data refinement and joint training.

sections.title: 2 Related Work
sections.content: Long-Horizon Multimodal Search. MMSearchR1 and WebWatcher train multimodal agents to interleave reasoning with external retrieval (Wu et al., 2025; Geng et al., 2025). Recent work extends search horizons and manages growing interaction histories (Huang et al., 2026; Du et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2026). DeepVoyager-VL uses intermediate visual evidence to guide subsequent search (Zhang et al., 2026b). These developments call for training questions requiring sustained, cross-modal evidence acquisition. Multimodal Search Data Construction. Questions solvable through parametric knowledge or short retrieval provide limited supervision for longhorizon search. Existing pipelines increase difficulty through multi-hop composition and entity obfuscation (Huang et al., 2026; Chen et al., 2026), graph-structured synthesis (Chu et al., 2026; Mei et al., 2026), and visual evidence integration (Zhang et al., 2026c,b). These constructions require evidence collection and validation. Our Refine pipeline reuses existing easy questions and candidate reasoning chains, applying Expand, Blur, and Visualize to control chain length, disambiguation, and visual requirements without building large graph from scratch. Reinforcement Learning for Multimodal Search. GRPO-based training improves search policies through interaction (Shao et al., 2024; Huang et al., 2026), but terminal scores offer limited feedback on partially useful trajectories. Process rewards, adaptive sampling, and finer credit assignment address this limitation (Chen et al., 2026; Yan et al., 2026; Dai et al., 2026; Jiao et al., 2026; Mei et al., 2025; Zhang et al., 2025). HyperEyes combines efficiency rewards with teacher distillation on failed rollouts (Li et al., 2026). Our joint optimization combines answer rewards and behavior penalties with reward-gap-weighted teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories, using exponential annealing to reduce reliance on the SFT teacher during training.

Each synthesized question is walked through from the input image, with minimal wording fixes to ensure solvability and answer uniqueness. We check chain consistency, evidence provenance, imagetext alignment, and actual use of the designated Blur and Visualize evidence. These checks approximate Equation 1 and help ensure that the added requirements in Equation 8 are non-trivial. Difficulty filtering and trajectory selection. We discard questions answered correctly by directanswer probe without tools. An expert model then performs tool-augmented rollouts per question using the training search-and-vision interface. Correctness controls eligibility, while the shaped reward gap controls strength. Being better than its peers does not imply that rollout reaches the target reward. Figure 5(a) shows mean answer reward before behavior penalties rising from 0.347 to 0.587 over 19 steps. Despite batch fluctuations, this trend indicates improved answer quality during joint RLOPD training. Search Behavior. Search trajectories initially lengthen and then contract (Figure 5(b)). Comparing steps 613 with steps 1419, average tool calls decrease from 26.0 to 21.3 (18.3%), and generated response length falls from 29.0k to 23.4k tokens (19.5%), while mean answer reward remains comparable (0.525 versus 0.544). These observations are consistent with increasingly economical search: later rollouts use fewer interactions and generated tokens without corresponding decline in average answer quality. These batch-level trends describe the joint training run rather than isolate the effect of individual components.

sections.title: 5 Conclusion
sections.content: We introduced MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint RLOPD training for long-horizon multimodal deep search. Refine reuses existing multimodal questionimage pairs and applies targeted transformations to control search depth, entity disambiguation, and visual evidence requirements. Joint training complements answer rewards and behavior penalties with reward-conditioned token-level guidance on imperfect student trajectories, while progressively reducing teacher influence. Across seven primary benchmarks, our 9B agent improves average accuracy by 15.3 percentage points over its agenticworkflow baseline, with joint training adding 2.3 points beyond SFT. Data ablations further support the training value of refined questions. Together, these results show the value of upgrading existing multimodal data to require sustained evidence acquisition. They also support joint outcome optimization and selective teacher guidance for learning long-horizon search and reasoning over text and images.

sections.title: Limitations
sections.content: Refine increases evidence requirements along designated reasoning chains, but filtering cannot rule out all shortcuts from parametric knowledge or alternative web evidence. Training depends on teacher and answer-judge quality, which may introduce noisy guidance. Open-web search also relies on changing content and tool availability, limiting reproducibility.
